signals.title: Ivory Coast Bets On Private Capital to Power New $209b Growth Plan
signals.summary: [Daba Finance] Ivory Coast's parliament has signed off on a new National Development Plan, mapping out the country's economic path through 2030. The centerpiece is an investment push of FCFA 114,838.5 billion, equivalent to roughly $209 billion or €175 billion, built around six pillars spanning security, agriculture, private investment, human capital, infrastructure, and governance. Unlike past cycles, the government wants the private sector to carry most of the load this…

signals.title: Rebels Seize Key-Town of Anéfis As Rebels Tighten Grip On Northern Mali
signals.summary: [RFI] Tuareg separatists and al-Qaeda affiliates appear to have secured control of a key town in northern Mali following a coordinated offensive by the rebels over the weekend. The Malian army and Russian mercenaries have been holed up in the key camp of Anéfis after the rebels launched their offensive on Saturday 4 July.

signals.title: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger Begin Formal Withdrawal From ICC
signals.summary: [Shabelle] Ouagadougou -- Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger have formally launched the process of withdrawing from the International Criminal Court (ICC) after submitting official notifications to leave the Rome Statute, according to a statement from the Assembly of States Parties to the court.

signals.title: World Bank Group Appoints Nicola Pontara As Division Director for Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali and Niger
signals.summary: [World Bank] Bamako -- The World Bank Group has announced the appointment of Nicola Pontara as Division Director for the Sahel countries - Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, and Chad.

signals.title: Senegal MPs Pass Reform Limiting Presidential Powers
signals.summary: [allAfrica] The parliament has approved controversial constitutional reforms that expand lawmakers' powers while limiting those of the president, deepening a growing rift between President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and parliamentary Speaker Ousmane Sonko.

signals.title: Mozambique: le nouveau Code minier impose une participation de l’État
signals.summary: Promulgué début juin, le nouveau Code minier impose notamment une participation de 15 % de l’État dans tous les projets miniers et inquiète les professionnels du secteur.

signals.title: Créer en langues africaines: les séries télévisées en pulaar [2/5]
signals.summary: La langue pulaar a désormais ses séries télévisées. Le secteur est même en développement et voit apparaître, en plus de petits producteurs isolés, des sociétés de production, comme la chaîne Marodi. À Dakar, Bokar Tall a assisté au tournage d'un épisode de Kaya, une toute nouvelle série en pulaar.

signals.title: Au Gabon, l'iboga, une opportunité dans la lutte contre la dépendance aux opiacés
signals.summary: Le Gabon souhaite tirer bénéfice d’un regain d’intérêt international pour l’iboga, dans le cadre de la lutte contre la dépendance aux opiacés, en particulier aux États-Unis. Les autorités ont récemment renforcé le cadre légal de l’exploitation de cet arbuste endémique symbolique du pays, car associé aux rites traditionnels. Ses promoteurs espèrent la formation d’une véritable filière pour contrer le marché noir.

signals.title: Police in South Africa open probe into post-World Cup death of Jayden Adams
signals.summary: The country's football players' union confirmed Adams's death on Saturday, but the cause has not been revealed.

signals.title: Ebola en RDC : le personnel de santé en grève pour salaires impayés
signals.summary: Des dizaines de personnes travaillant dans un centre de traitement d'Ebola à l'hôpital général de Rwampara, dans le nord-est du Congo, se sont mises en grève lundi pour protester contre le non-paiement de leurs salaires et primes.

signals.title: Sénégal : qui pour succéder à Pape Thiaw à la tête des Lions de la Teranga ?
signals.summary: Le Sénégal se cherche un sélectionneur après le limogeage de Pape Thiaw. Qui pour prendre la tête des Lions de la Teranga ? Les spéculations vont bon train.

signals.title: Statement by Foreign Affairs Minister of State Sola Enikanolaiye Receiving U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Frank Garcia
signals.summary: [MFA Nigeria] Abuja -- The Honourable Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, on Monday, 13 July 2026, received the United States Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, His Excellency Frank Garcia, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Abuja, where both sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the long-standing strategic partnership between Nigeria and the United States.

signals.title: U.S. Backs Nigeria to Prosecute Terrorism-Related Offences
signals.summary: [Leadership] The United States of America has thrown its weight behind Nigeria in the efforts to combat terrorism by ensuring a system that will effectively prosecute terrorism-related offences in the country as well as boost intelligence sharing.

signals.title: La transformation locale des minerais critiques africains au cœur d'un sommet à Abidjan
signals.summary: L'Afrique veut transformer davantage de ses minerais sur son sol, plutôt que de les exporter à l'état brut. À Abidjan, décideurs et industriels réfléchissent au développement de chaînes de valeur locales pour capter une plus grande part des richesses générées par ces ressources..

signals.title: Violences xénophobes  en Afrique du Sud : le Nigeria demande des réparations [Africanews Today]
signals.summary: De nombreux nigérians rentrés au bercail ont abandonné le fruit de plusieurs années de travail en Afrique du Sud.

signals.title: Pétrole : le Nigeria a produit plus que son quota Opep
signals.summary: Le premier producteur d’Afrique a atteint une moyenne de 1,56 million de barils de brut par jour en juin, son plus haut niveau depuis six ans.

signals.title: Mali: le Comité des disparitions forcées de l'ONU demande à Bamako de «localiser et protéger» Mountaga Tall
signals.summary: Au Mali, près de deux mois et demi après l'enlèvement, par la Sécurité d'État, de Maître Mountaga Tall, le Comité des disparitions forcées des Nations unies demande aux autorités maliennes de transition de « prendre des mesures immédiates pour rechercher, localiser et protéger » l'ancien ministre et défenseur de la démocratie. Une demande qui concerne également son fils, Cheick Mamadou Tall, enlevé à son tour deux semaines plus tard. C'est ce qu'indique le comité onusien…

signals.title: L’Afrique du Sud prévoit de stocker deux mois de réserves stratégiques de carburant
signals.summary: En pleine crise du détroit d’Ormuz et particulièrement affectée par les problématiques de prix et d’approvisionnement, l’Afrique du Sud souhaite revoir sa politique de réserves stratégiques de carburants.

signals.title: Dangote’s industrial empire is Africa’s shield against global shocks, says Afreximbank chief
signals.summary: Nigerian businessman Aliko Dangote’s investments are proving that African industrial giants can protect the continent from geopolitical crises and supply disruptions, says Afreximbank president George Elombi.

signals.title: Nigeria, South Africa row over compensation for deportees
signals.summary: Nigeria says it is collating details of its citizens who recently returned to the country to use them to demand compensation from South Africa, something Pretoria has ruled out

signals.title: Meurtre au Royaume-Uni : le principal suspect comparaît en Afrique du Sud
signals.summary: Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma, citoyen britannique d'origine zimbabwéenne, a comparu lundi devant le tribunal de première instance de Johannesburg, les yeux visiblement rougis, pour répondre d'une accusation de détention illégale d'une arme à feu.

signals.title: Le Nigeria réclame des indemnisations pour ses ressortissants rapatriés d'Afrique du Sud
signals.summary: Le Nigeria a indiqué collecter les renseignements relatifs à ses ressortissants récemment revenus d'Afrique du Sud, afin d’obtenir des indemnisations de la part du gouvernement sud-africain.

signals.title: Poverty Has Greater Impact On Brain Ageing Than Cancer, Study
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Poverty may have a greater influence on healthy brain ageing than a cancer diagnosis, according to a new study by the Aga Khan University Brain and Mind Institute (AKU-BMI), highlighting the role of socioeconomic conditions in shaping long-term cognitive health.

signals.title: My Greatest Fear Is Not Knowing When to Quit Music - Davido
signals.summary: [Vanguard] Afrobeats superstar David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, has opened up about what he considers his greatest fear, admitting that he worries about not knowing the right time to step away from music.

signals.title: Court Okays Trial of 4 for Hacking Into Firm's Bank Account
signals.summary: [Vanguard] ABUJA -- The Federal High Court sitting in Abuja, on Monday, gave the Inspector General of Police (IGP) the nod to arraign four persons for allegedly hacking into the financial records of a company.

signals.title: Terra Biga, une tontine 3.0 pour le Burkina Faso
signals.summary: Vous connaissez sans doute les plateformes de dons ou de financement participatif comme Leetchi ou Ulule… Au Burkina Faso, le créateur d’une jeune start-up a mis en place en 2024 un équivalent africain, « Terra Biga », qui permet de soutenir des projets et même de faire des économies par des achats groupés.

signals.title: Video - 'Abia, I'm Your Next Governor' - Actress Doris Ogala
signals.summary: [Vanguard] Nollywood actress and African Action Congress (AAC) governorship candidate for Abia State, Doris Ogala, has sparked reactions on social media after declaring that residents of the state have "no choice" but to accept her as their next governor.

signals.title: Rulaac Calls for Investigation Into Complaints Arising From Enugu North By-Election
signals.summary: [Vanguard] The Rule of Law and Accountability Advocacy Centre (RULAAC) has called for an independent investigation into complaints arising from the June 20, 2026, Enugu North Senatorial District by-election.

signals.title: Les indépendances africaines à l'honneur aux Rencontres d'Arles
signals.summary: Les Rencontres d'Arles ouvrent leur 57ᵉ édition avec un mot d'ordre : « Des mondes à relire ». Plus de quarante expositions, des artistes venus de tous les continents, un bicentenaire de la photographie, mais surtout une volonté affichée de regarder autrement notre époque, ses mémoires et ses fractures. Cette année, l’une des expositions-phares des Rencontres nous projette dans l’Afrique des indépendances. En 1957, le Ghana devient le premier pays d'Afrique subsaharienne…

signals.title: Court Orders Fresh Review of Kengen Carbon Credits Tender
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The Court of Appeal has ordered a fresh review of a disputed Kenya Electricity Generating Company (KenGen) carbon credits tender, ruling that procurement entities cannot introduce new evaluation criteria during the due diligence stage of a tender process.

signals.title: Tchad : début de la saison des pluies, la capitale menacée par des inondations
signals.summary: À N’Djaména, la capitale tchadienne, comme au début de chaque saison des pluies, les inondations menacent la ville. Les initiatives publiques et privées se multiplient pour éviter le plus de dégâts possibles, parmi celles-ci, le projet pilier, financé par la Banque mondiale, qui met en place des stations de pompage à N’Djaména. Explications d'Harold Girard.

signals.title: Ouganda : nouveau revers juridique pour l'oléoduc géant “Eacop”
signals.summary: Nouveau revers juridique pour l'oléoduc géant “Eacop”. Quatre agriculteurs ougandais, dont les terres sont directement concernées par le tracé de ce pipeline censé relier le pays à la Tanzanie, ont déposé cette semaine une action en justice devant la Haute Cour de Londres contre la société britannique qui porte le projet. Explications d'Aurore Bayoud.

signals.title: Tchad : N'Djamena, la capitale, se prépare pour la saison des pluies
signals.summary: À N'Djamena, la saison des pluies rime avec risque d'inondations. Pour mieux protéger la capitale tchadienne, les autorités et leurs partenaires déploient de nouvelles solutions, dont des stations de pompage financées par la Banque mondiale.

signals.title: Ebola en RDC: «Le combat à Kisangani est de limiter la mobilité et détecter tous les cas suspects», selon le ministre de la Santé
signals.summary: En RDC, la nouvelle a provoqué une grande inquiétude. Ebola a fait son entrée à Kisangani, la très peuplée capitale de la province de la Tshopo, où quatre cas sont confirmés. Ils viennent, selon les autorités, de Nia-Nia, une zone de santé de l'Ituri distante d'environ 350 kilomètres. Le ministre congolais de la Santé, Roger Samuel Kamba, répond aux questions de Patient Ligodi.

signals.title: Kenya : le phénomène des "goons" inquiète les ONG
signals.summary: Le Kenya connaît une recrudescence inquiétante de ces soi-disant "goons", ou voyous armés, engagés par des politiciens ou des groupes politiques pour mener une "répression informelle", selon certains défenseurs des droits de l’homme.

signals.title: Côte d'Ivoire : des dissidents demandent la démission de Tidjane Thiam de la tête du PDCI-RDA
signals.summary: En Côte d'Ivoire, nouvelle crise au sein du PDCI-RDA. Des militants dissidents réclament la démission du président du parti, Tidjane Thiam, qu'ils jugent trop absent. Ils demandent la tenue d'un nouveau congrès.

signals.title: Les manifestations anti-migrants pourraient affecter l'économie sud-africaine
signals.summary: En Afrique du Sud, les manifestations anti-migrants, alimentées par le chômage et la crise économique, font craindre des répercussions sur des secteurs dépendants de la main-d'œuvre étrangère.

signals.title: Ghana: 10 things to know about Sylvia Adusu, ITLOS’s first African woman judge
signals.summary: Her election as the first African woman to the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea is a landmark moment for her native Ghana and for the continent’s voice in global justice.

signals.title: Kenya: Rights groups warn of growing 'goon' culture
signals.summary: Kenya is witnessing a growing use of hired gangs by political actors to intimidate opponents, disrupt protests and silence dissent, rights advocates warn.

signals.title: Environ 60 000 migrants ont quitté l'Afrique du Sud depuis début juin
signals.summary: Plus de 38 000 ressortissants malawites ont quitté l’Afrique du Sud en l’espace d’un mois, dans un contexte de tensions croissantes visant les populations étrangères. Les autorités sud-africaines estiment qu’environ 60 000 personnes auraient quitté le pays depuis le début de cette période de crise.

signals.title: Ouganda: l’opposant Kizza Besigye forcé d’assister à son procès à la Haute Cour de Kampala
signals.summary: En Ouganda, le procès pour trahison de Kizza Besigye doit entrer dans le fond ce 13 juillet 2026. Cet opposant historique a été conduit de force devant la Haute Cour de Kampala, ce lundi. Accusé d'avoir comploté « pour renverser par les armes le gouvernement » ougandais, il est emprisonné dans son pays depuis son enlèvement au Kenya en 2024.

signals.title: France – Burkina Faso : Jean-Noël Barrot et Karamoko Jean-Marie Traoré, ministres au cœur de la rupture
signals.summary: La rupture entre Paris et Ouagadougou est désormais consommée. Aboutissement logique d’une crise diplomatique qui ne cessait de s’accentuer, elle a été prononcée, de part et d’autre, par deux ministres qui ne s’apprécient guère.

signals.title: The Dangote Effect and Nigeria's Energy Transition
signals.summary: [allAfrica] The global conversation on energy transition has gained remarkable momentum in recent years. Across continents, governments are setting ambitious targets to reduce carbon emissions, expand renewable energy, and ultimately achieve net-zero economies. Nigeria has not been left behind. Through its Energy Transition Plan and other climate commitments, the country has signaled  its intention to embrace a cleaner and more sustainable energy future.

signals.title: South Africa’s treasury closes the money tap to force municipal accountability
signals.summary: The National Treasury has temporarily frozen R13.5bn ($825.8m) in funding to 69 failing South African municipalities, drawing a hard line against financial mismanagement ahead of the November local government elections.

signals.title: Ouganda : le procès de Kizza Besigye débute après le rejet de son recours
signals.summary: En Ouganda, le procès de l'opposant Kizza Besigye débute ce lundi.  La Haute Cour a rejeté il y a quelques jours la demande de l'accusé visant à bloquer les poursuites pour trahison engagées contre lui et Hajji Obeid Lutale.

signals.title: Blow to South African corruption case as key suspect pulls out of plea deal
signals.summary: Vusimusi "Cat" Matlala could have given evidence against senior police officials in a $22m graft case.

signals.title: Gospel Outgrows Drill Among Kenya's Young Listeners As Nairobi's Gen Z Shapes a Multi-Genre Listening Culture
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi moves to the rhythm of its young people, and increasingly, that rhythm extends far beyond the music. From matatu rides and campus corridors to neighbourhood cafés, creative spaces and late-night hangouts, Gen Z is helping shape the soundtrack of everyday life. Their playlists accompany the daily hustle, while podcasts fuel conversations that stretch well beyond the music.

signals.title: SGR Cargo Volumes Rise 12.3pc
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The Standard Gauge Railway (SGR) transported 4.3 million tonnes of cargo in the first half of 2026, driven by stronger freight demand following China's introduction of duty-free access for most Kenyan exports.

signals.title: Uganda: Court clears way for Besigye treason trial
signals.summary: The High Court has dismissed an application by Dr. Kizza Besigye and Hajji Obeid Lutale seeking to terminate treason proceedings, clearing the way for their trial to begin on July 13, 2026. The court ruled the application lacked merit and was intended to delay the criminal case.

signals.title: Sifuna Emerges As Top Choice Among Gen Z Voters in Latest Infotrak Poll
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has emerged as the most popular political figure among Kenya's Gen Z voters, according to the latest Infotrak survey released on Monday, underscoring the growing influence of young voters ahead of the 2027 General Election.

signals.title: UDA Leads Party Popularity Poll As ODM Closes Gap, Infotrak Survey Shows
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA) remains the country's most popular political party, but the gap with the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) has narrowed significantly, according to the latest Infotrak Research and Consulting survey.

signals.title: President Tinubu Congratulates Kabir Shagaya At 40
signals.summary: [State Department] President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, has congratulated Mr Kabir Shagaya, Director of Strategy at Cavista Holdings, on his 40th birthday, commending his contributions to enterprise development, strategic investment, innovation, and national development.

signals.title: UK Backs Kenya As Regional Security Anchor, Eyes New Frontiers in Cyber and Ai
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The United Kingdom is deepening its security partnership with Kenya beyond traditional counterterrorism operations to tackle emerging threats including cybercrime, artificial intelligence (AI) risks and organised immigration crime, British High Commissioner to Kenya Matt Baugh has said.

signals.title: UK, Kenya Begin Talks On Landmark Digital Trade Deal to Boost E-Commerce, Tech Investment
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The United Kingdom and Kenya have begun negotiations on a landmark Digital Trade Agreement aimed at expanding cross-border digital commerce, reducing barriers for businesses and cementing Kenya's position as Africa's "Silicon Savannah," British High Commissioner to Kenya Matt Baugh has revealed.

signals.title: NPS Warns Political Actors Against Violence, Says No One Is Above the Law
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The National Police Service (NPS) has warned political actors and their supporters against engaging in violence and disrupting lawful gatherings, insisting that no individual or political affiliation is above the law.

signals.title: 19-Year-Old Woman Dies After Falling From Fifth Floor Building in Kayole
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Police in Kayole are investigating the death of a 19-year-old woman who fell from the fifth floor of a residential building in Nairobi's Kayole area.

signals.title: Macron reçoit Ramaphosa pour renforcer le partenariat franco-sud-africain
signals.summary: Le président français Emmanuel Macron a reçu vendredi à l’Élysée son homologue sud-africain, Cyril Ramaphosa, dans le cadre d’une visite officielle destinée à consolider les relations entre Paris et Pretoria.

signals.title: Fresh Fears in Oyo As Gunmen Kidnap School Headmaster
signals.summary: [Premium Times] Mr Owoade, who is also a member of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), was abducted around 6:00 p.m. on Saturday while returning home from his farm in Budo Aare, Itesiwaju Local Government Area of the state.

signals.title: Court Rules No Automatic Renewal for State CEOs
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The Court of Appeal has dismissed an appeal by former Kenya Reinsurance Corporation Managing Director Jadiah Mwarania, ruling that he had no automatic right or legitimate expectation to a third five-year term after the expiry of his contract.

signals.title: Gunmen Kidnap Oyo School Headmaster, Demand N30m Ransom
signals.summary: [Vanguard] A 60-year-old headmaster of Nomadic Basic School, Igbojaye, in Itesiwaju Local Government Area of Oyo State, Mr Matthew Kolawale Owoade, popularly known as "Onaiye", has allegedly been abducted by unidentified gunmen.

signals.title: Court Reserves Judgment in Suit Challenging Pantami As Gombe PDP Governorship Candidate
signals.summary: [Premium Times] Mr Pantami defected from the APC after losing out in that party's governorship primary, citing irregularities and injustice.

signals.title: High Court Summons Lenku in Amboseli Park Contempt Case
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Kajiado Governor Joseph Ole Lenku faces a possible six-month jail term after the High Court summoned him to appear on July 24 to answer contempt proceedings over allegations that he defied conservatory orders suspending the transfer of Amboseli National Park to the Kajiado County Government.

signals.title: Le Limpopo, miroir de la crise migratoire sud-africaine
signals.summary: Le fleuve Limpopo est devenu le théâtre d’un double mouvement migratoire : des exilés tentent toujours de rejoindre clandestinement l’Afrique du Sud, tandis que des dizaines de milliers d’étrangers repartent après une vague de violences xénophobes.

signals.title: US-Africa Week Ahead: Trump’s Africa envoy heads to West Africa as Washington courts Sahel juntas
signals.summary: Assistant Secretary of State Frank Garcia is travelling to Nigeria, Mali and Côte d’Ivoire for his inaugural trip to the continent, as the United States seeks to rebuild ties with the Alliance of Sahelian States.

signals.title: Premiers ministrables marocains : ceux que l’opinion plébiscite
signals.summary: Aucun d’entre eux ne dirige un grand parti, et certains n’ont même jamais exprimé leur désir d’occuper le poste de chef du gouvernement. Pourtant, leur nom revient avec insistance dès qu’il est question du Maroc de l’après 2026.

signals.title: Au Nigeria, l’érosion du littoral d’Orimedu menace les villages
signals.summary: Dans cette communauté côtière du golfe de Guinée, la montée du niveau de la mer, le changement climatique et la dégradation des sols accélèrent le recul du rivage. Une exposition itinérante consacrée aux solutions d’adaptation tente de sensibiliser les habitants et les décideurs.

signals.title: Ruto Tops New Presidential Poll At 32% As Kalonzo Comes Second At 13% - Infotrak
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- President William Ruto would retain the presidency if elections were held today, according to a new Infotrak Research and Consulting survey that places him ahead of his closest rivals in the race to State House.

signals.title: 14 Charged Over Kisumu, Nyahururu Violence As Police Vow Tough Crackdown
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Fourteen suspects have been arraigned over weekend violence in Kisumu and Nyahururu as the government faces growing pressure to demonstrate that its repeated pledges to end political goonism will be backed by consistent prosecutions rather than rhetoric.

signals.title: Plateau, Benue Killings - Nigeria Cannot Prosper While Innocent Blood Flows - Obi
signals.summary: [Vanguard] Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 election, has condemned the latest killings in Benue and Plateau states, saying Nigeria cannot achieve meaningful development while innocent citizens continue to lose their lives to violence.

signals.title: ICPC Arraigns Ex-Minister Uche Nnaji for Certificate Forgery, Misappropriation of Funds
signals.summary: [Premium Times] ICPC arraigned the 63-year-old Nnaji on six charges before Judge Joyce Abdulmalik of the Federal High Court in Abuja.

signals.title: Nigeria Meets 104% of OPEC Quota As Production Soars
signals.summary: [Premium Times] According to the crude statistics, released by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) on Sunday, in the month under review, crude oil production hit 1. 56 million barrels per day (mbpd)

signals.title: Ex-Minister Uche Nnaji Arrives Court to Face Arraignment for Certificate Forgery
signals.summary: [Premium Times] The ICPC is expected to arraign the former minister on charges of forgery and making false statements in documents submitted to public authorities.

signals.title: Ramaphosa honors South Africa's WWI fallen in France
signals.summary: Ramaphosa also called for greater recognition of Black South Africans whose contributions to the war were ignored for decades, saying the country's history should reflect the sacrifice of all who served.

signals.title: Senegal coach Pape Thiaw sacked after World Cup exit
signals.summary: Senegal's national footbal coach Pape Thiaw's functions were revoked in the night from Sunday to Monday. The decision is "in the best interests of Senegalese football", according to the Senegalese Football Federation.

signals.title: Nigeria : le soulagement des parents après la libération d'élèves enlevés
signals.summary: Au Nigeria, les enlèvements dans les écoles sont fréquents. Des groupes armés les prennent pour cible afin de faire pression sur le gouvernement et d’obtenir des rançons.

signals.title: Oyo Abduction - the Rescue Was Successful, but Where Was the Noise?
signals.summary: [Vanguard] When the news first broke that students and teachers had been abducted, the nation reacted as expected. Social media erupted with outrage. Television stations ran breaking news coverage. Newspapers led with banner headlines. Political commentators dissected the incident, while citizens demanded answers from the government and security agencies.

signals.title: Detained Oriire Terrorists' Wives May Face Trial, Calls Mount for Borno Pupils' Rescue
signals.summary: [Leadership] Some wives of suspected terrorists behind the abduction of schoolchildren and teachers in Oriire Local Government Area of Oyo State may face prosecution if ongoing investigations establish that they played active roles in the kidnapping operation, security sources have disclosed.

signals.title: Paul Biya et le Cameroun : d’un 13 juillet à l’autre, chronique d’une année folle
signals.summary: Le 13 juillet 2025, Paul Biya mettait fin à un faux suspense, déclarant sa candidature à la présidentielle, 43 ans après son arrivée au pouvoir. Le début d’une surprenante campagne électorale et d’une étrange année politique, à l’issue de laquelle la nouvelle ère attendue n’est toujours pas advenue.

signals.title: Govt Arrests Two Suspected Illegal Miners, Shuts Osun Mining Site
signals.summary: [Premium Times] According to the federal government, the suspects are assisting investigators to identify the sponsors of the illegal mining operation as authorities intensify efforts to curb unlawful mineral exploitation.

signals.title: Enhancing the Integrity of the 2026 Electoral Act
signals.summary: [Premium Times] Our federal lawmakers deserve a strong rebuke for these bizarre contrivances to the legislation taking us into the next general elections.

signals.title: CJ Koome Establishes High Court Division to Handle Tribunal Appeals
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Chief Justice Martha Koome has established a new Tribunals Appeals Division of the High Court at the Milimani Law Courts in Nairobi in a move aimed at improving access to justice and expediting the resolution of disputes arising from specialised tribunals.

signals.title: LSK Condemns Violence Ahead of Ol Kalou By-Election, Deploys Election Observers
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) has condemned all forms of violence, intimidation, incitement and lawlessness ahead of the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, warning that such actions threaten constitutional rights and democratic participation.

signals.title: Govt Moves to Suspend Sh6.9tn Public Debt Case

signals.title: Ivory Coast Completes IMF Program As Debt Risk Falls
signals.summary: [Daba Finance] Ivory Coast completed its economic program with the International Monetary Fund and was reclassified as being at low risk of debt distress, becoming the only sub-Saharan African country with that status.
